summary: A common fungal leaf disease of strawberry. Many small purple spots merge until leaves look scorched, weakening plants and reducing fruit.
symptoms: Many small (1-5 mm) irregular purple to reddish-brown spots on the upper leaf
Spots have no light centre and fuzzy borders
Leaves dry out and look scorched; margins may curl up
key_sign: Many small dark purple spots with no pale centre and indistinct borders.
favourable_conditions: Warm, wet weather; long periods of leaf wetness; perennial (matted-row) plantings.
spread: Overwinters on infected leaves; spores spread by splashing water.

today: Remove and destroy badly scorched leaves
this_week: Switch to drip irrigation or water early in the day so leaves dry quickly
If many plants are affected, apply a fungicide registered for strawberry leaf spots
next_two_weeks: Thin crowded plants and runners for airflow

chemical: Captan and other fungicides labelled for strawberry leaf spots (often already part of fruit-rot programmes)
cultural: Renovate beds after harvest and remove old leaves
Rotate plantings and avoid overhead irrigation

prevention: Plant resistant cultivars and certified disease-free transplants
